phase: Wave 3 — gauntlet rounds on the built game
headline: Round two of the blind A/B moved the town from losing 10-0 to 'clearly behind, but the gap is one ground-plane pass wide — the assets are already competitive and were being wasted on the surface they sat on'. Buildings-integrated now scores for us. The conformity act is fully wired with its authored dialogue, the Memory Threads board no longer grades the player, and audio ships with the hand bell provably quoting the tower.

findings.text: Dry grass and bare soil were declared as base families, painting hard tile-aligned rectangles across the whole map — a blind A/B read them as a rendering bug. Now blob overlays with organic boundaries.
No prop cast a shadow — the critic called adding them 'the cheapest single improvement in the whole list'. The world builder now drops one under every prop that stands up, sized from the sprite.
Two villagers wore clothing within a few luminance points of the grass at nearly the same hue, so they camouflaged. Moss now separates by value, sage by hue, Oren's olive by value.
All 236 authored lines are wired and the didactic inline version is gone; the naming moment is now the recognition version. The trial's answers match what the villagers say about it afterwards.
The reference lantern always played tone A, so in rounds where the answer was B or C the perceptual task was unsolvable by ear.

The Memory Threads board graded every placement, printed a score, and volunteered the answer. Now a placement is a claim; ENTER commits the whole board, and a refusal returns a physical fact rather than a verdict.
shrine_boss hangs the renderer on load — never produces a frame, 30s timeout. Blocks the whole-game playthrough harness.

A dead zone in the upper-middle grass band measures the lowest structural energy in the frame; that is where the square wants to be. Plus uniform-width paths, a path that dissolves into grass, a store with no door, and ~12 identical trees at the same orientation.
Doors are narrower than the characters who must walk through them.

The journal rendered only definition, illustration and terms — misconception, real-world examples and every example the player earned were written and never displayed, tilting the notebook toward a vocabulary list. Now two pages: what happened to you first, formal terms second.

Cut a naming-moment line that told the player they had learned, a Sera idle line that gave away the whole first puzzle before the player had tried it, and an insight-card eyebrow that asserted the player's inner state.

A session token limit terminated nine in-flight agents mid-edit. Four partial edits were repaired (Web Audio typed-array generics, a half-written event helper, an unexported map symbol); all agents resumed from their transcripts rather than restarting.
Phaser getFrame() returns the __BASE frame for unknown names, so every missing-art guard was drawing the entire 2048px atlas across the scene.

comparisons.title: Town Square vs Stardew Valley world density
comparisons.verdict: Round 2: clearly behind, but the critic's own summary is that the gap is one ground-plane-and-lighting pass wide, not an art-quality pass. Buildings-integrated-vs-dropped-on now scores for us, and it named our lit windows, roof variety and prop sophistication as ahead of the reference.

comparisons.title: Festival Plaza vs Stardew Night Market
comparisons.verdict: The event transformation reads: string lights, bunting, a lit ceremonial carpet, stalls and a gathered crowd. Trial lanterns still need mounts.
